text:
anna: spun up the PHX2 baremetal racks this morning, all nodes passed hardware health but I saw some weird p95 spikes during the initial throughput probe
pranay: saw the same in the smoke run. p95 jumps to ~420ms for a subset of requests while median stays ~65ms
liam: what model/config were you running in the probe?
anna: running the standard perf-harness v2: batch_size=8, seq=512, continuous batching on, model=falcon-40b-quant. kernel: Ubuntu 22 + nvidia-driver 535.54, cuda 12.3
pranay: attached the perf log -> link: https://internal/runs/phx2/1769501234/results (perm: infra-team)
amelia: quick note: a few nodes reported nvlink errors in dmesg during burn-in, marking node-07 and node-12 for follow-up
liam: can you paste the relevant dmesg snippet?
anna: sure:
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, pid=2345, reason: GPC stall
[  123.456800] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
```
pranay: that Xid 79 usually correlates with driver/kernel mismatch or bad firmware. Which kernel version?
anna: 5.15.0-112-generic with our standard boot params (nosmt quiet).
pranay: compare with the validation matrix: PHX2 infra requires kernel >= 5.15.0-120 for the 535 driver to avoid the GPC stall on certain Ampere variants. That mismatch could explain the p95 spikes
amelia: interesting — our baseline clusters use driver 560 + kernel 6.x. Did we intentionally pin 535?
liam: we pinned 535 for compatibility with our quantized runtime earlier, but recent runtime patch removes that dependency. I can test 560 on a couple of nodes
anna: action: I'll cordon node-07/12 and reprovision kernel to 5.15.0-128 and driver 560 on a canary pair
pranay: also run a quick microbench: grpc vs http for single-token latency; we've had differences when grpc session multiplexing interacts with kernel socket buffers
amelia: here's the quick perf command I used locally for single-GPU baseline:
```
./perf-harness --model falcon-40b-quant --batch 1 --seq 64 --mode single-token --transport http --iters 5000 --log p95
```
liam: thanks. also add `--enable-nvlink-check` (new flag) so the harness reports cross-GPU NVLink saturation metrics
anna: after reprovisioning, I ran the canary pair with driver 560 + kernel 5.15.0-128. Results:
- median latency: 62ms (unchanged)
- p95 latency: 74ms (from 420ms)
- throughput (tokens/s per GPU): 11,600 -> consistent with expected baseline
pranay: that's promising — confirms driver/kernel mismatch was the main culprit
amelia: what's left for full handoff? we need a staged roll of the kernel+driver change across the PHX2 fleet, plus a health probe and a cost check for any perf delta
liam: rollout plan suggestion:
1) Canary (2 nodes, done)
2) Small batch (10% of GPU nodes) over 2 maintenance windows with perf probes after each batch
3) Full fleet in waves of 25% with automated rollback on p95 > baseline*1.4 or token throughput drop > 8%
pranay: define probes: for each wave run:
- perf-harness smoke (batch sizes 1, 8, 16; seq 64/512)
- nvlink check
- kernel logs scan for Xid/IO errors
- network egress sanity (no sudden egress cost spike)
anna: created infra ticket INFRA-2319 with the plan and attached the canary artifacts
amelia: small callout on cost: driver 560 enables some kernel-level batching improvements that reduce per-token CPU overhead, we should expect slight CPU drop — good for cost but watch for any memory pressure on the nodes
liam: also check the compilation cache warmup step in the runtime, sometimes new drivers invalidate GPU-side JIT caches causing a short-term throughput dip during first hour after rollout
pranay: added a one-hour soak probe that continuously hits the fleet after each wave and reports rolling 15m p95 + tokens/s. If p95 drift > 10% for more than 20m, auto-kill wave and rollback
anna: logs from the problematic node before reprovisioning:
```
2026-02-21T08:14:03Z WARN kernel: nvlink: dropped packet count=32
2026-02-21T08:14:03Z ERROR runtime: kvcache: fallback hit (miss ratio 0.21)
```
amelia: kvcache fallback rate looks high on those nodes. That could amplify p95 when combined with NVLink stalls
liam: follow-ups assigned:
- anna: finish fleet roll plan + INFRA-2319 updates (ETA EOD)
- pranay: extend perf harness with `--nvlink-sat` and add the one-hour soak alert (ETA tomorrow morning)
- amelia: run cost delta simulation for driver 560 (ETA Wed)
- liam: prepare rollback playbook and automated job (ETA EOD)
pranay: I'll add a small synthetic that toggles `continuous batching` off/on to measure sensitivity; helps decide safe rollout thresholds
anna: thanks team. tagging @sre-bot to start the canary postmortem summary into the incidents channel once the ticket lands
sre-bot: Canary completed: 2 nodes reprovisioned -> metrics stable. Summary uploaded to https://internal/incidents/INFRA-2319/canary-summary (auto-generated) :white_check_mark:
liam: once PRs for the harness and soak rules merge, we can schedule the first maintenance window. I'll open the calendar invite
amelia: thumbs up. small reminder to add firmware verification to the runbook — NVLink issues sometimes persist even after kernel/driver bump if GPU firmware is old
anna: noted, adding firmware check step to the runbook (FW version >= 94.3 required)
pranay: closing note: this thread proves value of quick microbench + nvlink telemetry early in bring-up. let's add an explicit NVLink health gate in the phx2 runbook
anna: agreed — updating the runbook now and will link in INFRA-2319
liam: thanks all, moving to implementation
